objective: Help business owners compare invoice finance against a traditional bank overdraft for managing cash-flow gaps.

slides.headline: What's the real difference?
slides.body: An overdraft is a set limit attached to your bank account, available regardless of your invoicing activity. Invoice finance advances funds specifically against unpaid invoices, meaning the amount available can scale up automatically as your sales and invoicing grow.

caption:
An overdraft is simple and familiar, but it's also fixed — the limit doesn't move just because your invoicing volume does.

Invoice finance is built to scale with your sales, advancing funds against invoices you've already issued rather than sitting at a static limit. For B2B businesses on 30-90 day terms, that difference can matter as volume grows.
